title: Mode-selective nonlinear interference for high-brightness and high-purity fiber-coupled SPDC sources
authors: Carlos Sevilla-Gutiérrez, Purujit Singh Chauhan, Varun Raj Kaipalath, Fabian Steinlechner
abstract: Single-mode-fiber-coupled spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) sources are a key resource for photonic quantum technologies, but in single-crystal geometries brightness, heralding efficiency, and spectral purity remain constrained by intrinsic trade-offs. Here, we show how nonlinear interference in a cascaded two-crystal type-II SPDC source can be used to engineer the modal structure of SPDC emission, improving the brightness--heralding-efficiency trade-off by more than one order of magnitude beyond the single-crystal limit. We further demonstrate two routes to near-unity spectral purity while retaining high brightness and/or heralding efficiency, even with standard periodically poled crystals, and study the additional advantages of aperiodic poling with Gaussian phase matching. Using a spectrally resolved Laguerre--Gauss modal decomposition, we show that these improvements arise from mode-selective interference of spatial-spectral SPDC modes within the nonlinear interferometer. We experimentally validate the model through sum-frequency-generation measurements of the spatial-spectral state.
summary: This paper presents a method to drastically improve the performance of fiber-coupled SPDC sources by exploiting mode-selective nonlinear interference in a cascaded two-crystal setup. The technique overcomes inherent trade-offs between brightness and heralding efficiency by more than an order of magnitude. Both theoretical modeling using Laguerre-Gauss modes and experimental validation via SFG confirm that this architecture enables high-purity, high-brightness quantum light sources.
main_problem: The primary challenge is overcoming intrinsic trade-offs (brightness vs. heralding efficiency vs. spectral purity) in single-mode-fiber-coupled Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC) sources.
main_result: By utilizing nonlinear interference in a cascaded two-crystal setup, the authors demonstrate an improvement of over one order of magnitude in the brightness–heralding efficiency trade-off while maintaining near-unity spectral purity.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling using spectrally resolved Laguerre–Gauss modal decomposition with experimental validation via Sum-Frequency Generation (SFG) measurements.
model_or_system: The system is a cascaded two-crystal type-II SPDC source. The analysis models the process by incorporating nonlinear interference effects across both spectral and spatial degrees of freedom using Laguerre-Gauss modal bases.
key_observables: Pair-collection probability (Brightness), Heralding efficiency, Spectral purity ($P$), Joint Spectral Amplitude (JSA).
important_parameters: The improvement factor is $>10$-fold; high heralding efficiency ($H \geq 0.97$) and spectral purity ($P > 0.99$) are key targets.
main_assumptions: Initial analysis uses the plane-wave approximation, but results extend to complex spatial modes using LG decomposition; the enhancement relies on dispersion compensation in the cascaded structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between single-crystal and two-crystal PMFs, showing interference effects that suppress sidelobes and enhance performance. Experimental setup diagrams detail the use of tunable lasers and nonlinear crystals for measurement.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the fundamental trade-off in SPDC sources to developing a theoretical model based on nonlinear interference in cascaded systems. It then quantifies the improvement over single-crystal limits, discusses spectral/spatial mode decomposition, and concludes with experimental validation using SFG measurements.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of quantum light sources by engineering complex spatio-spectral correlations through nonlinear optics, which has direct implications for quantum communication protocols.
